newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks fall as shares go ex-dividend.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks fall as shares go ex-dividend.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell to a five-month low on Tuesday, pushed lower by more shares going ex-dividend this week.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.38 percent to 150.46 points, its lowest level since November, in turnover of just 403,000 dinars ($569,000).
Jordan Islamic Bank and Jordan Phosphate Mines which both resumed trading after going ex-dividend, slipped nearly five percent to 3.62 dinars and 3.05 dinars.
Arab Potash, which announced a 0.2 dinar dividend at its annual general meeting on Wednesday, was not traded but is expected to fall when it resumes trading.
Another blue-chip share, Jordan Petroleum, is expected to increase its dividend by 10 percent to 0.89 dinars next month.
Brokers say the market may need another two weeks before it shakes off the downward pull of the ex-dividend shares.
"After the effect of the dividends it will go up to the same levels as before," said one broker. The official AFM index has eased around five percent since February.
Jordan National Bank, which merged earlier this year with the Business Bank, fell to 1.73 dinars on Tuesday, its lowest level since the merger.
Brokers said investors who had waited for the merger were gradually offloading the stocks.
Overall falling shares in the official market outnumbered gainers by 14 to 13, with another 15 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.26 percent to 79.95 points, 4.13 percent down from the start of the year.
